name: Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend
signature: void Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend(void* cameraMgr, const float* blendDuration, const float* offsetVec3)
summary: Stores a 3-float focus offset (0.0, 2.5, 0.0 when offsetVec3 is NULL) in the camera manager's +0x84..+0x8C follow-camera block, asks the camera child at f_40 to re-blend with *blendDuration and clears the +0x90 mode byte. Used by talk-zoom, cutscene and battle-UI camera code when the focus moves to a new speaker/target.
evidence: FACTS.md already ties 0x002AE144 to the camera child f_40 and the focus offset at +0x84..+0x8C; the six named callers (TalkZoomCameraEnable, Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera, Battle_Ui_UpdateStateMachine, Text_MessageWindow_Update) all move/reset the camera focus around a speaker change, and the only callee is maybe_Camera_UpdateYawSpring on f_40.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAndReleaseCutscene
summary: Message-window close path: notifies the overlay helper 0x001DBB34 through the scene-transition manager, releases the cutscene message and camera at self+0x70 (Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera / Cutscene_Teardown) and finishes the UI-core transition with the message id at f_b0+0x146.
evidence: The body is fully readable through named callees and its real work is the cutscene release at self+0x70; nothing releases a speaker/face icon, so the old 'WithSpeaker' wording was unsupported. Sibling 0x0019F554 is the same close path with a different first notification.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseAndNotifyCharacter
summary: Second close path of the message window: notifies the 2D field character handler (Field2D_OnCharacterChanged) with the window owner and message id, then releases the cutscene message/camera at self+0x70, tears the cutscene down and finishes the UI-core transition. Identical to 0x0019EA58 except for that first notification.
evidence: Same named teardown chain as 0x0019EA58 (Cutscene_ReleaseMessageAndCamera, Cutscene_Teardown, Ui_SmithMenu_FinishTransition) with Field2D_OnCharacterChanged as the only difference; there is no emote/line handling in the body, so the old 'CloseWithEmoteLine' name was a guess.

name: Battle_OrientActorAndGetGroupMidpoint
summary: Computes the 3D midpoint/direction across the active opposing units in the action sequence's 16 unit slots (+0x70), orients the acting unit model through Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection and writes the resulting world position to outPosVec3. Used by the battle actor action, name popup and member-anchor code.
evidence: All four named callers need a world-space group position (Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor, Battle_ActorAction_ShowNamePopup, Battle_Actor_Update, Battle_ActionSequence_Update); the loop counts non-null entries in the 16-slot table, averages their bounds with Math_ComputeBoundingSphere and passes the direction to Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection. The second argument is the float[3] output, as the full-ARM evidence states.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_Step_PostUnitMessage
summary: One step of the battle UI state machine at self+0x125C (state 0xCDB): posts battle message 0x1B for the acting unit through Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry, in 3D also resolves the popup anchor with Battle_Ui_GetMemberAnchor, waits for the actor queue to drain and then moves to state 0xCEE/-2. It creates no visual effect.
evidence: The only payload built is a Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry record whose message id comes from the data row 0x1B (Game_GetDataManager + func_0063E05C); there is no effect-creation call, so 'ShowMemberHitEffect' had no support. The state layout (0xCDB -> 0xCEE/-2, Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty gate) matches the named sibling step 0x0047F600.

name: Battle_InitWork
summary: Initialises the battle work: lazily creates its 0x194-byte, 15-state sequence sub-object (vtable 0x0075A888, per-state ctor 0x006C4350) and then sets up the shared unit list at +0x4254, the five 0x40-byte party slots at +0x1C, the four 0x1C-byte unit lists at +0x428C and the 3D/2D unit model tables at +0x4330/+0x47A0.
evidence: FACTS.md identifies +0x4254/+0x4270/+0x428C/+0x4298 (stride 0x1C), +0x4330 (3D) and +0x47A0 (2D) as battle-work fields, and the tail of the body initialises exactly those with maybe_Field_InitSharedParams and func_002AB618; the only caller (0x0019ECE4) passes self->f_5C, which FACTS calls the battle work. Nothing in the body touches field objects, so 'Field_InitObjectTable' was wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_SetupSpriteFromRecord
summary: Configures a sprite child of a UI part from a record: copies the owner/palette ids (f_B4/f_B0/f_AC), creates the sprite actor and its priority, plays the record's animation (clamped to 0..6), builds the 9-slice/frame-colour descriptor from the record rectangle and adds the child through Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild.
evidence: All eight callees are now named sprite helpers (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Gfx_LookupSpritePriorityByte, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, Gfx_CreateFColAnimator, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild), which confirms the 'set up a sprite part from a record' reading; the class owner is still a factory/table slot with no caller, so the Ui_Part prefix stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_SetupFourSpriteParts
summary: Same record-copy head as 0x0061A5C4 (owner/palette ids at +0xAC/+0xB0/+0xB4, sprite actor creation and animation), but then builds four 0x48-byte sprite part sub-objects at +0x298 with Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, taking the animation id straight from desc+0x18.
evidence: The callees are sprite/2D helpers (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, maybe_Gfx_Sprite_BuildFootprintRect) and the loop constructs four child parts; there is no animation-model call, so the old 'Model_InitWithFourAttachedParts' name described the wrong object type.

name: maybe_Field_MarkerWidget_UpdateScreenPos
summary: Converts the widget's local rectangle at +0x2E0 into a screen position by subtracting the field object's camera offsets f_78/f_7C, then resolves the resulting position id (0xFF = none) and applies it through Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation on that object.
evidence: The rectangle/camera-offset subtraction is clear, but the id resolver 0x00319678 is a split symbol inside Ui_PastScenarioWindow_Dtor (0x0031961C), so its meaning is not confirmed; the class name MarkerWidget still comes from the first pass, hence kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Gadget_OnNotify
signature: void maybe_Field_Gadget_OnNotify(FieldGadget* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Notification callback of a field gadget: when the gadget's mode byte f_297 is 2 it forwards the gadget's f_2EC id to the shared field scene object's animation setter (Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation on work+8->+0x54->+0x20). The notification parameters are unused.
evidence: Only callee of substance is the named Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation and the f_297==2 gate is clear, but the gadget class and what event 2 means are still unknown and the function has no direct caller (vtable slot).

name: maybe_Gfx_Trail_UpdateInterpolated
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Trail_UpdateInterpolated(int unitIndex, u32 frame, int flags)
summary: Second trail follow-path update variant: interpolates the trail origin between two key frames (with a cubic segment evaluation), recomputes the segment length and the active flag at f_1C5 and applies the result to the trail node's path.
evidence: The body is damaged decompilation (coprocessor_store, unaff_r5/r6, in_d8/in_d9, in_s20) so even the argument order is unrecoverable; the callee set matches the trail update at 0x5F41AC, which is all that supports the 'trail' reading, so it stays a maybe_ at low confidence.

name: maybe_Camera_FollowIndexUpdate
summary: Per-frame update of the follow camera: accumulates the hold timer, when it expires toggles the mirror flag through the owner's virtual +0x90 and asks maybe_Camera_FollowSelectNext for the next follow index, then compares the current grid delta (f_78/f_7C) with the target to derive a turn direction for the owner's +0xC4/+0xC8.
evidence: The only named neighbours are maybe_Camera_FollowSelectNext and a scene animation setter; the timer and the mirror toggle are readable but the direction fields (+0xC4/+0xC8) are still inferred, and the function has no caller in the batch (per-frame virtual slot), so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_SetSlotState
signature: void maybe_Model_SetSlotState(void* model, u32 slotId, int state)
summary: Sets/clears the per-id state flag on a battle model: for a non-zero state it validates the id through the data-manager record and may rebuild the unit's action list, then special-cases ids 0x75/0x76/0x88..0x8F/0x11B (unlink from the parent lists), clears the 0x121-entry arrays at +0x124 and +0x5E0 and the f_8EE pending byte, and calls func_00279FB8 four times for that id.
evidence: Callers show the second argument is a small id in the 0..0x120 range: Menu_RefreshUnitSlotFlags loops all 0x121 records and passes the index, BattleScene_RefreshCommandWidgets passes 0x9A/0xDB/0x9C after testing the same id on the unit's vtable+0xE8, and Actor_NotifyComponentEvent passes an event id. That makes the +0x124/+0x5E0 arrays per-id state tables rather than a single 'slot', but whether the id is a unit id or a state id is still unclear, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_StateSequence_LazyCreate
summary: Lazily creates the owner's 0x134-byte sequence object the first time it is needed: allocates it, installs vtable 0x0075ABA0 and its secondary table at +0x98, stores the owner back-pointer and constructs the 11 (0xB) 0x18-byte states with 0x006C8980.
evidence: The vtable's methods are std_StateSequence67_ChangeState/Tick/SetState/Delete, the per-state ctor passed to std_ConstructArray is 0x006C8980 and the count is 0xB, so the created object is a state sequence, not a child scene node; the body never accesses a scene-node child list, which makes 'Gfx_SceneNode_EnsureChild' misleading. Which owner/subsystem it belongs to is still inferred from the session-init caller.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CtorB
signature: void maybe_Ui_DiveForm_CtorB(u32 object, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Second constructor variant of the dive-form window hierarchy: calls the confident Ui_DiveForm_Ctor, installs the derived vtable, initialises the member pair and constructs its 19 (0x13) 0x18-byte state array. The B suffix only distinguishes it from the other ctor variant at 0x003096D4.
evidence: The recovered body calls the named Ui_DiveForm_Ctor and Ui_Object_InitMemberPair and uses vtable 0x0075ABC4; both ctor variants have identical call shapes, so which derived class each one belongs to is still unresolved and the name stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_StampBookWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the stamp-book window: reinstalls vtable 0x007655A4, releases the five part handles at +0x44..+0x54, the model handle taken from work+0x54, resets the draw group, clears the two gfx-context flags and releases the pack handles.
evidence: The installed vtable 0x007655A4 matches its sibling Ui_StampBookWindow_DeletingDtor, and every release call is now named (Ui_List_ReleaseEntries, Pack_ReleaseHandle, Ui_Widget_DetachAndDestroy, Gfx_ResetDrawGroup); the only remaining damage is Ghidra's 'unreachable block' removal, the released fields are all visible.

name: Party_FindNextEntryForCharacter
summary: Advances a party character-entry cursor to the next matching 0x14-byte row of the data-manager table: row charaId 0xFF or equal to cursor->u8_00, story-flag bit set in GameWork+0x2A444, map-visited byte at +0x27508, quest state 9 and party condition opcodes 0x19..0x22; sets the cursor index to 0x7FFFFFFF when exhausted.
evidence: All three confident callers are Party_* helpers (Party_GetFirstActorForCharacter, Party_GetActorNoForCharacter, Party_BuildUsedCharacterList) and they use the returned cursor protocol; the table row fields (+0x08 story flag, +0x0A map flag, +0x0C quest, +0x10 charaId) are the same ones maybe_Party_FindEntryByType reads. It walks party character entries, not live Actor objects, so the Actor_ prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_Group_BuildFromString
summary: Resolves a party/battle member specification (a type char plus an index byte, with a special 'R' form) into an id: checks the party size at GameWork+0x27218, maps the spec through func_004A4AD0 / func_004A5498 and tests the member's learned skills and offhand weapon state. The decompiler hit bad instruction data, so the spec grammar is only partly recovered.
evidence: The body carries 'Control flow encountered bad instruction data' and uses undeclared globals; the named callees Party_CountLearnedSkills and Party_Member_HasOffhandWeapon show it tests member state, but 'Group_BuildFromString' still overstates what is proven. Only two callers exist (Battle_BuildUsableSlotMask, maybe_Ui_EntryArray_Build).

name: Party_FindEntryByType
signature: u32 Party_FindEntryByType(u32 partyCtx, u32 arg2, int member, u32 type)
summary: Walks a party member's character-entry cursor (Party_GetFirstActorForCharacter + Party_FindNextEntryForCharacter) until it finds an entry whose condition field f_12 equals `type`, returning that entry's id f_11, or `type` itself when the list is exhausted. Member index 3 is first resolved by scanning the party for character id 0x1B.
evidence: Eight confident callers across battle UI and field code (Battle_UiFlow_EvaluateCondition, Battle_TargetMarker_CollectSlotFlags, Battle_CommandListWindow_BuildEntries, Ui_TsuyosaWindow_SortMembersByStat, Field_Actor_ApplyWeaponAnim) use it to map a condition type to a party entry id, and the iteration is exactly the named cursor protocol of Party_FindNextEntryForCharacter/Party_EntryMatchesSelectedId.

name: Battle_Ui_FinishActorMessage
summary: Single-state step of the battle party panel: resolves the action row for the actor id at self+0x497, posts that actor's model-actor popup entry (state 0x274B), waits for Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty, sets the battle-work byte +0x424B, clears the actor's UI flag through Menu_ClearActorUiFlag and ends the step (-2 / state 0x2758).
evidence: Its vtable 0x00774680 also holds the named Battle_Ui_ResolveCommandResult and Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel, and the body's only payload is Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors with the actor id at self+0x497; the command-list/menu-object guess in the first pass is gone.

name: maybe_Battle_RollHitRateByTemplate
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_RollHitRateByTemplate(void* actionTemplate, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Resolves the action's 0x1D-class combat-modifier entry from an 8-entry template (0x2C stride, entry kind at +0x58), computes the chance with Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers and compares a 1..100 battle-RNG roll against it; returns 1 when the roll passes. The real parameters were dropped by Ghidra (the body still references arg2/arg3).
evidence: The named callee Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers produces the threshold and func_001CA474(battle RNG, 1, 100) rolls the check, while the 0x2C-stride table is scanned for kind 0x1D; that confirms a hit/proc roll, but the 'ByTemplate' wording is still an interpretation and the dropped parameters keep the signature honest as maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_CheckTargetReceivesAction
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_CheckTargetReceivesAction(u32 actionId, u32 unitArg, void* target, void* result)
summary: Decides whether an action can resolve against a target: returns 0 with a failure code in result+4 when the action row blocks it, when the target carries state 0x6F/0x70/0xFF, or when it is status-immune; otherwise computes the action's chance modifier and returns 1 only if a 1..100 battle-RNG roll is within it.
evidence: The action row comes from the named func_0063FD24 (FACTS: action rows), the vtable +0xE8 tests are unit status ids 0x6F/0x70/0xFF, the callee maybe_Monster_IsImmuneToStatus is a status immunity test and the tail is the battle-RNG threshold roll; the callers (Battle_ActorAction_ShowDamage, Battle_Ui_UpdateMessageSequence) treat the result as 'action proceeds'. There is no monster-specific or message-row code, so the old 'Monster_CheckRowState' name was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_RollActionStatusChance
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_RollActionStatusChance(u32 actionId, u32 unitArg, void* target, void* result, int variant)
summary: Rolls an action's status-effect chance against a target: resolves the action row (or the SkillRecord it points at), computes the chance with Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers, compares a 1..100 battle-RNG roll, then calls maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc and tests the target's immunity; sets result->f_54 and returns 1 when the status lands.
evidence: The named SkillRecord wrapper func_0018C1B8 (f_CE variance, f_DE/f_E2/f_CC) and Battle_ResolveMemberCombatModifiers, plus maybe_Battle_RollStatusProc and the vtable +0xF8 check, show a status-application roll; the only caller Battle_Ui_ShowActionEffectMessage consumes the result as 'status applied'. The old 'RollActionRowSuccess' name described text rows, not this.

name: maybe_Field_MapJumpJob_Poll
summary: Polls a small field job (state byte +0x45): states 0/1 report the script trigger manager's busy flag (work+8->+0x6C), state 2 fires Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent(0x3FF, self->f_46) once the manager is idle and then pauses the player and the UI objects matching mask 0x40000040 while the map jump runs.
evidence: The only event the state machine fires is Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent with the job's f_46 as target, and the Ui_ObjectList_Begin/End walk pauses objects with the 0x40000040 mask; nothing in the body is a generic 'interaction', so the old InteractJob prefix was a guess. No direct callers (job table).

name: maybe_Battle_PickUnitNearAverageLevel
summary: Chooses a random candidate among the 0x413 entries of the work+0x2857C table whose level (record+0xC) lies within about +/-30% of the average party level; the action id in desc+0xC selects one of four weight tables which pick a sector (0..3, returned in the high word) and the battle RNG then picks the final entry.
evidence: Reading the body item by item: func_0035EB98(...)->f_D8 (member level, FACTS) is averaged, the accepted band is average +/- 0.3*average, and the scan keeps entries where func_0063DCA4(...)->f_C lies in band; the four weights come from func_0063D178 and are consumed with a 1..100 battle RNG. Callers (Model_CreateActorModel) store the low word into a model id field, so this is unit/monster selection, not the 'weighted candidate' pick the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Sys_InitCommandRings
signature: void maybe_Sys_InitCommandRings(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int padMask)
summary: Initialises a render-session object: fills two 256-entry command rings with their entry pointers, starts each ring's mixing state and gfx command ring (one per 3DS screen), stores the screen parameters and then builds the 16-button pad mapping from the pad table at +0x35C.
evidence: Gfx_InitCommandRing and Snd_InitMixingState are called once per ring (rings at +0x35C/+0x790 and +0x1BCC/+0x2000) and the tail maps 16 mask words into three pad words via func_00112448; the _Reset/_IRQ/_FIQ register names in the tail are damaged Ghidra output, so the exact pad semantics stay unproven.

name: maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb
signature: void maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb(int mode, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Thumb-mode copy of the pad-mask mapping block that also appears at the end of maybe_Sys_InitCommandRings: maps the raw button masks through the 16-word table into three output words and posts them through func_0010E8D0.
evidence: Same constant sequence and func_00112448/0x00112450 helpers as the pad block of 0x00108C5C, but the entry is Thumb and the body is damaged (unaff_r5/r7/r9/r11, in_s0), so the argument order and even the parameter count are unrecoverable.

name: maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker(u32 arg1, u32 mask, int count, u32* d, int header, int* state)
summary: Normalises a command-list state counter modulo 8 and validates the list header/count before copying command payloads; the decompiler hit bad instruction data at the first branch, so only the header check is trustworthy.
evidence: The body contains 'Bad instruction - Truncating control flow' and halt_baddata(), and the only listed caller (Input_ReadPadState) is a table neighbour rather than a real call; no named callee clarifies the format, so the name stays a guess.

name: Gfx_WaitForIpcIdle
summary: Waits for the GPU IPC command queue to go idle: after the optional 0x400/0x200 capability queries it calls the 3-state helper and polls Gfx_IpcCmd3B0040(argument) with 10 ms sleeps until the answer leaves the three busy/error codes (0xC8A0CFF0, 0xE0A0CC08, 0xC8A0CC02), then negotiates the display mode.
evidence: All three IPC wrappers are now named (Gfx_IpcCmd90040, Gfx_IpcCmd3B0040) and the callers are the gfx sync-submit/wait and sound update paths; the loop's three compared constants are status/error results, and a successful exit runs maybe_Gfx_NegotiateDisplayMode, so 'wait for the gfx IPC to become idle' describes the body.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateItemMenuWidget
summary: Factory for the 0x1170-byte item-menu widget: allocates from the UI heap, runs the Ui_ItemMenu_CreateRoot constructor (0x0019BDC4), attaches it through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, activates it (vtable +0x24) and marks it running (f_25=1); on part failure it releases the block. Reached from a table, no direct callers.
evidence: The constructor call is the named Ui_ItemMenu_CreateRoot (0x0019BDC4) and the attach/activate tail is identical to the sibling factory 0x002BBEB0, so 'ListWidget' understated which widget is built; the allocation size is now documented in the summary instead of the name.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateDialogWidget
summary: Factory for the 0x594-byte dialog-root widget: allocates from the UI heap, runs the Ui_DialogRoot_Init constructor (0x0019CBF4), attaches its parts through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, activates it and marks it running; on part failure it releases the block.
evidence: The ctor call is the named Ui_DialogRoot_Init and the attach/activate tail matches maybe_Ui_CreateItemMenuWidget; no direct callers (table-reached), so the class identity still rests on the ctor name.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNamePlate(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Creates once and shows the 0x260-byte plate window owned at self+0x18: runs the Ui_TimeWindow_Ctor class constructor, attaches its parts, sets its visible byte f_94, broadcasts to the children and switches the owner into two-plate mode (f_40=2).
evidence: No direct caller (vtable slot); the +0x18 attach and the two-plate store are unchanged, but the ctor is now named Ui_TimeWindow_Ctor, so the plate class is a time/name window rather than a generic nameplate; the exact purpose is still inferred, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenSystem_Rebuild
summary: Rebuilds the 0x328-byte screen-system object when the requested mode byte is 8: releases the old object through the UI core, allocates a new one, runs maybe_Field_CreateScreenSystem(block, self+0x1C), creates its parts and activates it; on failure the new block is released and the slot at self+100 is cleared.
evidence: Every callee is named (Ui_GetCore, Mem_AllocAligned_2, Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable, func_0021F8B8) and the mode-8 gate plus the release/recreate/store flow are clear; the class name still rests on the maybe_Field_CreateScreenSystem ctor, so kept maybe_.

name: Gfx_EntryPool_Clear
summary: Empties a gfx scene entry pool: walks the occupancy bitmask at +0x18 and for every live 0x34-byte entry unlinks and frees its sprite list, node list and the two list heads through the named Gfx_Scene_Delete*/Destroy* helpers, clearing the bit as it goes. Called from Field_DestroyScene.
evidence: The caller is Field_DestroyScene and all five callees are the named Gfx_Scene_DeleteSpriteEntryList/DeleteNodeEntryList/DestroySpriteList/DestroyNodeList helpers, so the pool belongs to the gfx scene rather than battle popups; the only damage left is one unaff_r9 temporary (damaged decompilation), the bitmask/unlink/free flow is intact.

name: Field_ReleaseResources
summary: Teardown helper: virtual-destroys the two optional owned objects at +0x14 and +0xC (slot +4 of each vtable) and returns self; called from Field_DestroyScene as the field's member-release pass.
evidence: The disassembly shows two guarded vtable+4 destructive calls and a plain 'return self'; Field_DestroyScene (named) is the only caller, and the earlier 'returns self+8 / status flag' reading was a decompiler artifact.

name: maybe_Field_CreateSpriteActor
summary: Creates the field's sprite actor (sprite 0x13E, layer 1): builds the 2D sprite descriptor, allocates 0x298 bytes from the field actor manager's allocator, constructs it with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630 and vtable 0x00726418, registers it in the field actor list and places it at the scene camera's x/y, replacing and releasing the previous handle.
evidence: The descriptor is a sprite descriptor (Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh + Field_SceneObject_ClearPartFlag) and the result is registered as a field actor with a shadow part, so calling it a scene *effect* was unsupported; there are no callers (table/factory), so the actor's purpose stays uncertain and the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact
signature: FieldSceneObject* maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact(void* heap, int* def, int arg3, int ctx)
summary: Field scene-object constructor: builds the base with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x0075EFDC (+0x98 secondary), caches the actor-manager pointer from work+0x54 twice, sets the 0xFF 'none' ids and chains three 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef members at +0x2EC.
evidence: The named callee Actor_HandleRef_Ctor confirms the three handle references, Os_GetGameWork confirms the two work+0x54 caches, and vtable 0x0075EFDC is the same family as the named Field_SceneObject_CtorC; the class name is still inferred, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorWithChildren(u32 owner, int descriptor, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor reached from a factory table: builds a 0x4000000C-tagged object with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x007591FC (+0x98 secondary), sets the 0xFFFF/0xFF sentinels and default-constructs four 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef children at +0x2A4.
evidence: Same constructor shape as maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorCompact (0x0028E630 + secondary vtable at +0x98 + 0x48-byte Actor_HandleRef children), and the four children are its distinguishing feature; the old 'vt1A59E4' suffix was an address fragment, not a class name.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorType7
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_CtorType7(u32 factory, int record, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor variant for a type-7 field scene object (model id 0x9DB): builds it with the shared actor factory 0x0028E630, installs vtable 0x0075F214 (+0x98 secondary), sets the 0xFFFF/0xFF sentinels and writes f_92=7 and f_A5=0x9DB.
evidence: The body calls func_0028E630 once, installs the vtable and writes the type/model ids; there is no child-creation call and no caller, so the old 'CreateTypedChild' name was wrong - it constructs the object itself.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_ShowSelectionResult
signature: void maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_ShowSelectionResult(UiItemScreen* item, int screen, char* flags)
summary: Validates the item/quantity currently selected on the item screen and posts the matching message: refuses with message 0x26 when the bag count plus the selected quantity would exceed 99, otherwise uses the item record's equipment range/flags to choose message 6/7/8 (equipment) or 5/0x20 (normal/stack) and activates it.
evidence: The body never modifies the bag: it only reads the bag entry (work+0x24ACC), Item_LookupRecord and the equipment id ranges from FACTS, then calls func_001C0F28 with message ids and Ui_ActivateScreenMessageAndModel. Callers Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput and Ui_ItemScreen_SelectQuantity use it to display the outcome, so 'CommitSelection' overstated it.

name: maybe_PartyStatus_ApplyToRecords
summary: Writes a cached party snapshot back into the live save: copies the 0x274C-byte bag block and the +0x24AC0 word, then for every slot with a non-0xFF character id restores the member's HP/MP, level/EXP, equipment and six inventory slots, re-applying each recorded item through Member_RemoveItemAtSlot/maybe_Member_SetItemAtSlot.
evidence: The named Party_Member_* calls and the GameWork+0x24AC0/+0x24ACC bag copies match the snapshot saver 0x00210044 field for field, so the data direction (snapshot -> live records) is clear; *when* it runs (save load vs. menu cancel) is still unknown, hence kept maybe_.

name: maybe_MenuActor_ApplyModelOverride
summary: Applies the 12-word model-attachment override block at 0x007E7110 to the menu actor's scene-sprite set: fetches the set from self+8, resolves the override by the id in arg2 through Model_Attach_ApplyOverrideByName and, on success, calls func_0061E700 with the same block.
evidence: The named callee Model_Attach_ApplyOverrideByName resolves the override by name/id and the 12-word block is copied from the static 0x007E7110 table; there is no animation-play call in the body, so 'PlayAnimation' described the wrong operation. The only caller Menu_InitFromParams passes the shared model manager at work+0x88.

name: maybe_PartyStatus_SaveSnapshot
summary: Saves the live party state into the snapshot block unless f_424A is set: copies GameWork+0x24AC0 and the 0x274C-byte bag block, then for each of GameWork+0x27218 members stores the actor id and the member's HP/MP, level/EXP and six equipped-slot item ids into a 100-byte per-member slot.
evidence: Field-for-field mirror of maybe_PartyStatus_ApplyToRecords, and the named Party_IsMemberActive / func_006292F0 / func_006297C8 reads supply exactly the HP/MP, level/EXP and equipment values that the apply side restores; when the snapshot is taken is still inferred, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplyActorModelPattern
signature: void maybe_Menu_ApplyActorModelPattern(MenuState* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: When f_424A is set, walks the four actor lists and for every slot record with a non-zero pattern id applies it to the actor's model through vtable +0xA0, copies the companion value into the model's +0x12/+0x16, then asks the scene transition controller (work+0x74) to refresh.
evidence: Only caller is Menu_InitFromParams and the only named callee in the path is Os_GetGameWork plus 0x002AEA84 on work+0x74; the +0xA0 model getter and the f_34E4/f_34E6 id pair are consistent with a model appearance/pattern, but nothing proves what the id selects.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateC
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateC(u32 layer, u32 owner, u32 value)
summary: Updates one slot of a 4-layer ownership table: under lock 0x007C865C, when the slot's owner word changes to/from 0 it adjusts the global owned-layer count, then stores the owner word and the caller-supplied value for layer 0..3. Copy C shares its lock with copy D.
evidence: Callers always invoke all four copies with the same layer and two value words (Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init layer 1 with a code address, Ui_LoadIconTextures layer 3, Gfx_ResetRenderer and the sound-shutdown paths). The stored owner/value pairs look like an ownership/borrow registry, but what the four tables gate is still unproven, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateD
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateD(u32 layer, u32 owner, u32 value)
summary: Fourth copy of the 4-layer ownership-table update (table 0x007C86BC, lock 0x007C865C): adjusts the owned-layer count when the owner word changes to/from 0, then stores the owner and the caller-supplied value for the given layer.
evidence: Same caller set and arguments as copy C (Gfx_MoviePlayer_Init, Ui_LoadIconTextures, Gfx_ResetRenderer, the two sound shutdown paths) and the same lock 0x007C865C; the table role is still inferred from those callers, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateA
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateA(u32 layer, u32 owner, u32 value)
summary: First of two 4-layer ownership tables sharing lock 0x007C8668 (table 0x007C8698): keeps the owned-layer count, stores the owner word for the layer and a second caller-supplied value, ignoring no-op changes.
evidence: Callers always update A and B together with the same layer, and movie/icon shutdown bind layers 1/3 with code addresses as one of the two values; that is consistent with an ownership registry, but its consumer is still unknown, so kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateB
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetLayerStateB(u32 layer, u32 owner, u32 value)
summary: Second of the two 4-layer ownership tables sharing lock 0x007C8668 (table 0x007C8674): byte-identical to copy A, keeps the owned-layer count and stores the owner word and caller-supplied value for layer 0..3.
evidence: Same caller set as copy A and byte-identical body apart from the table base; the arguments show the second word is an owner pointer/address rather than a boolean. What the pair of tables gates is still unproven, so kept maybe_.

name: BattleAi_ChooseActionSlot
signature: int BattleAi_ChooseActionSlot(void* aiCtx, void* targetCtx, int isPrimary)
summary: Chooses one of the six action slots of the current actor's tactics plan: collects the six slot weights from the tactics-weight table indexed by aiCtx+0xC, drops empty/excluded slots and then picks by weight (modes 0..6), by rotating index (7), by a rotating two-slot window (8) or by lowest non-empty slot (9); returns the chosen slot index.
evidence: FACTS.md places 0x0026B9EC inside the 0x00269F64..0x00277700 BattleAi block; the only caller BattleAi_SelectActionForCurrentActor then evaluates record + slot*0xE + 0xA as a spell id via the SpellRecord getter 0x0063CFC8. The 0xE-stride record holds five u16 condition ids plus one action byte and two flags per slot - not recipe ingredients - so the old Ui_RecipeBook_ChooseRecipeLine name misread the slot table.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWidget_ShowCurrentRow
summary: Shows the row the list widget's cursor currently points at: reads the cursor (f_D6C) and count (f_D70), fetches the 8-byte row record from the table at f_D84, applies the record's enable/height bytes and height class, pushes message command 9 and displays the record through Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord.
evidence: The body only touches the list widget's cursor/count/record fields (f_D6C/f_D70/f_D84) and the named Text_PushMessageByte/Text_PushMessageFlags/Ui_Widget_ShowWithRecord calls; the same row-showing tail also appears in the message-command handler 0x003B4EC8, so the shop attribution came from one caller only and the widget class is still inferred.
